question: What happens to your policy if your insurer fails?
answer: A domestic insurer does not ordinarily enter the same federal bankruptcy process as an industrial company. State insurance law, the domiciliary commissioner and a supervising state court instead control conservation, rehabilitation or liquidation. Liquidation normally triggers the guaranty duty; financial distress alone does not. Coverage, limits, residency and product eligibility are state-law questions. The guaranty system does not make every creditor whole, insure the insurer, or convert failure into a federal bailout.

groups.label: The failure constitution, section by section

items.title: State receivership replaces ordinary corporate bankruptcy
items.sub: Domestic Insurer Failure, Receivership and Policy-Continuity Constitution
items.text: The exclusion in 11 U.S.C. §109 preserves the state insurance-resolution perimeter. Under state receivership law, a court can appoint the insurance commissioner as rehabilitator or liquidator and place the legal entity's assets, operations and claims under court supervision. NAIC Model #555 supplies a coordinated model but has force only through state enactment and binding orders. Administrative supervision, conservation, rehabilitation and liquidation are different states. A low RBC ratio, examination finding, consent order or supervision agreement is not itself a liquidation. The receivership-court order identifies the authority, entity, effective time and powers.
kv: DOMESTIC_INSURER_FAILURE_RECEIVERSHIP_AND_POLICY_CONTINUITY_CONSTITUTION_2026-10-01.md, section “1. State receivership replaces ordinary corporate bankruptcy”

items.title: Rehabilitation and liquidation pursue different outcomes
items.sub: Domestic Insurer Failure, Receivership and Policy-Continuity Constitution
items.text: Rehabilitation attempts to correct the insurer's condition or restructure its obligations under a court-approved plan. Liquidation winds down the entity, fixes claim procedures and activates guaranty mechanisms where statutory conditions are met. A rehabilitation can fail and convert to liquidation, but that later order has its own date and consequences. The receiver must identify assets, policies, claim files, service providers, reinsurance, collateral, separate accounts, litigation and creditors. The record problem is operational as much as legal: policy and claim data have to be made usable by the guaranty associations and replacement administrators before continuity can work.
kv: DOMESTIC_INSURER_FAILURE_RECEIVERSHIP_AND_POLICY_CONTINUITY_CONSTITUTION_2026-10-01.md, section “2. Rehabilitation and liquidation pursue different outcomes”

items.title: Guaranty associations are statutory post-failure mechanisms
items.sub: Domestic Insurer Failure, Receivership and Policy-Continuity Constitution
items.text: NAIC describes guaranty mechanisms in all states and the District of Columbia, with product and territorial differences. Life/health mechanisms can continue eligible contracts or support transfer to a solvent insurer. Property/casualty funds pay eligible covered claims under state limits and exclusions. Liquidation normally triggers the guaranty duty; financial distress alone does not. The receiver and guaranty association have different duties. The receiver administers the estate for all recognized claims under state priority law. The guaranty association performs the bounded obligations created by its own state's statute and then may assert claims in the estate. A guaranty payment does not decide every coverage dispute or establish the estate's final recovery.
kv: DOMESTIC_INSURER_FAILURE_RECEIVERSHIP_AND_POLICY_CONTINUITY_CONSTITUTION_2026-10-01.md, section “3. Guaranty associations are statutory post-failure mechanisms”

items.title: Continuity depends on data, administration and transfer—not only money
items.sub: Domestic Insurer Failure, Receivership and Policy-Continuity Constitution
items.text: The NAIC receivership model calls for pre-liquidation coordination and transmission of policy and claim information, including counts, reserves, values, loans, premiums, litigation and third-party-administrator arrangements. For P&C failures, the model specifically contemplates preparing electronic policy and claims data for transfer using uniform standards. Life and annuity obligations may be continued, reinsured or transferred; P&C claims may move to guaranty-fund administration while policies terminate or are replaced under governing law and orders. Notice, data transfer, claim assumption, policy transfer, scheduled benefit and actual payment are separate continuity clocks.
kv: DOMESTIC_INSURER_FAILURE_RECEIVERSHIP_AND_POLICY_CONTINUITY_CONSTITUTION_2026-10-01.md, section “4. Continuity depends on data, administration and transfer—not only money”

items.title: The protection is financed after failure through the surviving market
items.sub: Domestic Insurer Failure, Receivership and Policy-Continuity Constitution
items.text: State guaranty associations generally assess member insurers after a covered insolvency, subject to statutory classes, bases and annual caps. The economic incidence can move again: state law may permit premium-tax offsets, policy surcharges or pricing recognition. The timing of assessment authorization, collection, payment, tax offset and policy-price recovery must be kept separate. NCIGF's assessment-liability reporting shows why this is an accounting chain as well as a legal one: surviving P&C insurers estimate obligations under state accounts before all cash assessments are final.
kv: DOMESTIC_INSURER_FAILURE_RECEIVERSHIP_AND_POLICY_CONTINUITY_CONSTITUTION_2026-10-01.md, section “5. The protection is financed after failure through the surviving market”

items.title: Estate recovery determines the final loss
items.sub: Domestic Insurer Failure, Receivership and Policy-Continuity Constitution
items.text: The receiver pursues cash, investments, reinsurance recoverables, collateral, affiliate claims, litigation and other rights. Guaranty associations can receive estate distributions or assert subrogated claims. Claimants outside guaranty coverage remain dependent on the estate and statutory priority. Separate accounts, secured creditors, federal claims and reinsurance setoff can create distinct legal questions. Gross guaranty payments therefore are not the final cost of failure. Final loss requires assessment cash, permitted recoupment or tax offsets, estate distributions, reinsurance collection, administrative expense and the uncovered policyholder/creditor shortfall.
kv: DOMESTIC_INSURER_FAILURE_RECEIVERSHIP_AND_POLICY_CONTINUITY_CONSTITUTION_2026-10-01.md, section “6. Estate recovery determines the final loss”

items.title: State insurance commissioners
items.sub: Distress & authority · Primary legal-entity supervisors of the business of insurance
kv: License, examine and enforce against domestic insurers; control reserves, capital, material transactions, dividends and receivership under state law.
The domiciliary commissioner controls the licensed legal entity; other states retain market and consumer authority within their laws.
State primacy does not eliminate federal securities, benefit, financial-stability, tax or public-program authority.

catalog_context.title: How insurers invest trillions, move risk and share losses with government
catalog_context.answer: U.S. insurance runs through many separate regulators, very large insurer balance sheets, reinsurance and public loss programs that together work as one system. Each authority, company, contract and payment still keeps its own legal identity and timing.
